system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Hybrid supervision: synthetic-lesion masks plus real-image MIL
SUMMARY: Train the segmentation adapters with Dice + Focal on synthetic lesions pasted into normal source images and with the problem's top-k MIL on real image-labelled abnormal images, never loading an expert mask.
HYPOTHESIS: Hybrid supervision exceeds both synthetic-only and MIL-only training by at least 1.5 held-out pixel-AUROC points and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: synthetic-only, MIL-only and hybrid supervision. With probability 0.5, a normal source image receives a synthetic lesion (patch from another normal image of the same dataset, Poisson-blended, 1-10% of the foreground) and its mask is used with Dice + Focal; real abnormal images use top-k MIL (k = 1%); real normal images supervise all patches as normal. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Synthetic anomalies come with exact masks at zero annotation cost, but alone they teach a model to find artefacts that look synthetic; real abnormal images with image labels carry realistic appearance but no location. A hybrid objective — Dice and Focal on synthetic anomalies, top-k MIL on real abnormal images — may give localisation that is both precise and realistic.
METHOD: 1) dataset/synthetic.py: wrapper around the training dataset that inserts synthetic lesions into normal images (p = 0.5) and returns their masks. 2) train_zero.py: seg loss = Focal + Dice on synthetic masks + lambda_MIL x topk_mil on real abnormal images (lambda_MIL = 1); real masks never loaded. 3) Hyper-parameters as released; lambda_MIL in {0.5, 1, 2}; insertion probability {0.25, 0.5}.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; synthetic-only; MIL-only. Falsified if hybrid is not better than both single-signal variants.

Idea B:
TITLE: DINOv2-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
SUMMARY: Refine the MIL-trained patch maps of abnormal source images by propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph and use the result as pseudo-masks for MVFA's Dice and Focal losses.
HYPOTHESIS: DINOv2-refined pseudo-masks increase held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over the unrefined MIL maps and over CLIP-affinity propagation, while image AUROC changes by less than 1 point.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: pseudo-mask refinement (none; DINOv2 affinity propagation; CLIP-feature affinity propagation). Stage 1: top-k MIL (problem statement). Stage 2: for each abnormal source image, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features on a grid matched to MVFA's, affinity A_ij = max(0, cos)^8, row-normalised; m' = (0.7 A + 0.3 I)^3 m; pseudo-mask = m' > 0.5 max(m'). Stage 3: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask IoU (analysis), pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Image-level MIL localises a handful of the most anomalous patches. DINO features are spatially coherent, so a random walk over a DINO patch-affinity graph can grow MIL evidence into region-shaped pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters densely, with DINO used only offline during training.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1: loss.py topk_mil in train_zero.py. 2) New script refine_masks.py: torch.hub DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (frozen), patch features resized to MVFA's patch grid, affinity and propagation in torch; save masks. 3) Stage 3: existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every source image (normal: empty). 4) DINO is not used at test time; inference cost unchanged. 5) Hyper-parameters: alpha 0.7, beta 8, t 3 (ablation alpha {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, t {1, 3, 5}).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only; CLIP-affinity propagation. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea A directly addresses MVFA's loss formulation by integrating complementary weak supervision signals (MIL on real labels and exact masks on synthetic lesions) into a single end-to-end training loop without adding external vision foundations. In contrast, Idea B introduces a disjoint, multi-stage pipeline relying on an external, frozen DINOv2 model whose patch affinity assumptions are generic rather than specific to MVFA's multi-level adapter and text-anchor architecture. Furthermore, Idea A is significantly more testable and lightweight within the constrained Colab GPU setting.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
